blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 5 killings of trans people (trans women and people of a local trans-feminine identity category) in 2025, sharing the 5-killings band with two other states. Against a population of ~7.2 million the rate is about 0.69 per million per year, roughly 1.8x the national figure (~0.38: 80 killings across ~211 million people). The state/province sits on a dry agricultural frontier, and the national monitoring dossier finds 67.5% of the country's trans killings occur in interior cities outside the capitals - where monitoring, reporting and access to public policy are weaker - so a visitor away from the capital shares this interior exposure.

No local ordinance, legal restriction or protection measure was identified in the dossier; the profile rests on the above-national per-capita killing rate and the interior-concentration pattern. The companion 2024 national dossier (122 killings, 16% below 2023) recorded the same ~68% outside-capitals share.
blindSourceSummaries: The national trans-murder monitoring association's ninth annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by a broadcast outlet): the country recorded 80 murders of trans people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; 2025 per-state counts in descending order - 8, 8, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims were trans women (including a local trans-feminine identity category), over half aged 18-29, 70% black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; the country has led the global ranking since 2008. Lists this state/province among the 5-killings states for 2025.

Coverage of the association's 2024 dossier (27 Jan 2025): 122 trans people (trans women and the local trans-feminine identity category) were murdered in the country in 2024, 16% below 2023's 145 and just under the 2008-2024 average of 125; five victims were human-rights defenders, including a city-council alternate; 95.9% of victims were trans women (including that category); the highest 2024 state counts were 16, 12 and 11, with three states recording none; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 1,179 killings confirmed 2017-2024; official statistics are unreliable due to misclassification and underreporting. Provides the 2024 national figures (122 killings, 16% below 2023) alongside which this state/province's 2025 figures sit.
